Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic

Class AgenticAdHocProcessEnginePlugin

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.cfg.AbstractProcessEnginePlugin
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic.AgenticAdHocProcessEnginePlugin
All Implemented Interfaces:
ProcessEnginePlugin
public class AgenticAdHocProcessEnginePlugin extends AbstractProcessEnginePlugin
What an agentic ad hoc sub process needs from the engine: the parse listener that recognises one, the handler that runs a turn, and the retry of a failed turn.

Lives here rather than in the generic connect plugin, where it sat while this was being built. A connector is found through ServiceLoader<ConnectorProvider> and cannot register either of these itself — that needs a process engine plugin — so the agentic machinery ended up in the one plugin every distribution already registers. The cost was a generic plugin that knew about AI, and AI hooks in every engine that uses connectors at all.

ConnectProcessEnginePlugin now looks for plugins a connector declares, with the same classloader it loads the connectors with, so this one is picked up without a single distribution configuration changing. Declared in META-INF/services/org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.cfg.ProcessEnginePlugin.

An engine without this module on the classpath therefore has no agentic hooks at all, rather than hooks that do nothing. A model carrying the agent's connector on an ad hoc sub process then deploys as an ordinary ad hoc sub process, which waits for its children to be activated from outside and is driven by no agent — the same outcome as before, reached without the engine carrying the machinery.

One piece is the exception, on purpose (CIB7-2136): the expression function toolParameter, with which a tool declares a parameter in its input mapping, is registered by ConnectProcessEnginePlugin, not here. An expression binds its functions when a model is parsed, so a model using it has to parse on an engine without this module too, and a definition deployed earlier has to load after the agent was switched off. There the function only hands its value on; a tool activated from outside that reads toolCall must be given one, since without this module no scope keeps an empty one.

No switch of its own (CIB7-2145): agentic ad hoc sub processes are on and off with the AI agent connector, because this plugin ships in its jar and is found with its classloader — on CIB seven Run AI_AGENT_ENABLED, --production and --ai, on Tomcat lib-ai on the common.loader, on WildFly the optional import of the ai-agent module by the connect plugin's module.xml. Switched off they go quietly, unlike an AI agent service task, which fails with "No connector found": a model asking for an agent deploys as a plain ad hoc scope, and an agent waiting for a tool when it was switched off ends with its last answer once that tool ends.
